title: Patti Corbett to receive Peggy Calhoun Memorial Site Surveyor Award
summary: Site surveyors are the foundation of the CAMTS accreditation process, evaluating medical transport services against standards that protect patients and crews.
body_markdown:
The Commission on Accreditation of Medical Transport Systems (CAMTS) is pleased to announce that Patti Corbett, RN, BSN, FAASTN, CISM, has been named the recipient of the Peggy Calhoun Memorial Site Surveyor Award. The award will be presented at the CAMTS Site Surveyor Reception on October 25, 2026, in Fort Worth, Texas.


The Peggy Calhoun Memorial Site Surveyor Award honors a CAMTS site surveyor whose commitment, expertise, and integrity reflect Peggy Calhoun’s legacy. Site surveyors are the foundation of the CAMTS accreditation process, evaluating medical transport services against standards that protect patients and crews.


Corbett has served CAMTS as a site surveyor for 33 years. Her service to the commission also includes a term on the CAMTS board of directors, representing the Air & Surface Transport Nurses Association (ASTNA), and a tenure as CAMTS Associate Executive Director.


Corbett, a flight nurse with more than three decades in critical care transport, is senior clinical advisor for Life Flight Network, where she leads initiatives focused on patient safety and clinical excellence.


She co-chairs the Association of Air Medical Services (AAMS) Patient Safety & Quality Committee and the ASTNA Publications and Education Committee, work that strengthens safety culture and advances high-reliability practices nationwide. Throughout her career, she has led multiple critical care transport services and patient safety programs.


“Patti has devoted more than three decades to the CAMTS site survey process, and the standards our accredited services meet today bear her fingerprints,” said Jan Eichel, executive director of CAMTS.


“She brings a clinician’s eye, a surveyor’s rigor, and genuine care for the crews and patients behind every program she visits. There is no one more deserving of an award bearing Peggy Calhoun’s name.”


*This press release was prepared and distributed by the Commission on Accreditation of Medical Transport Systems.*
